title: The channel join becomes rank-aware, and pipelineResult converges
description: mergeEntries resolves a duplicate id by canonical order, under which every settled status sorts before the seeded "proposed" — so the channel keeps the planned copy and a pge run reports a contract still marked "proposed" inside completedSprints. Switch to the rank-aware join already shipping in the same module. This closes the pipelineResult divergence, so the two-directional pin must be edited deliberately here.

successCriteria.description: mergeEntries resolves duplicates with rankIsGreater rather than joinByCanonicalOrder. No new ranking logic is introduced — versionRank and rankIsGreater are reused exactly as they ship.
A test proves the settled contract outranks the seeded "proposed" one, so a pge run no longer reports "proposed" inside completedSprints.
The latent lastWriteWinsByKey defect is fixed and pinned: attempts:10 must outrank attempts:9, which canonical order got backwards.

ORDER-INVARIANCE IS PRESERVED — the property appendById exists for. A test merges the same containers in several different arrival orders and asserts an identical result. This is the criterion most likely to be broken silently by a ranking change.

The pipelineResult conformance divergence is CLOSED, and conformance.engines.test.ts's divergence-set pin and its per-field record are edited DELIBERATELY in the same commit as the docs/pge-graph.md disposition they change.
Any golden case whose recorded artifacts move is re-captured in THIS sprint, with the diff verified confined to the contract status/version and their direct consequences.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green; golden gate passes with the replay count at or above its floor.

nonGoals: Weakening a pin to accommodate the change — the pin moves because the behaviour legitimately changed, and it must still fail in both directions afterwards.
Closing the contracts, history or audits divergences.
stopConditions: Order-invariance cannot be preserved under the rank-aware join — stop and report, because that property is why appendById exists.
A divergence other than pipelineResult moves — that is unplanned and must be understood before committing.
definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
generatorNotes: The change itself is one line at reducers.ts:187. Everything else is proving it safe. rankIsGreater's total order is version, then updatedAt, then canonical JSON — the last term is what keeps it deterministic when the first two tie, which is what preserves order-invariance. Say in the code why that fallback matters. For sc-4-5, remember the discipline the previous spec established: a pin edit and the doc disposition it changes go in ONE commit, never as a side effect.
evaluatorNotes: sc-4-4 is where a subtle break hides. Do not just run the generator's test — construct your own containers, shuffle them into several orders, and confirm identical results including when ranks TIE. Then verify sc-4-5 by reading the pin diff: it should record pipelineResult closing, not merely drop it. Confirm the divergence set is now exactly what a real run produces by running the harness yourself.
